  "text": "At four o’clock, the clock above the alterations counter struck thirteen. Mara looked up with a pin between her teeth. The clock had no chime; she had worked beneath it for eleven years.

Across the shop, Mrs Vale continued examining the hem of her black skirt.

“A little shorter,” she said. “I won’t be getting any taller.”

Mara took out the pin. “Did you hear that?”

“The traffic?”

Outside, a bus sighed against the kerb. Someone dragged a crate over the pavement. Ordinary sounds, arriving separately.

“Never mind.”

She marked the new hem in chalk and promised the skirt for Thursday. After Mrs Vale left, she climbed onto the stool and lifted the clock from its hook. The battery compartment was empty.

Of course it was. The clock had stopped in February. She had kept meaning to buy a battery.

Mara put it back and finished her work without looking up again.

When she closed the shop, an apple lay in the gutter beside her bicycle. It was small and hard, with a rusty seam running from the stalk. The trees at home had grown apples like that. Eli called them stitched apples and insisted they ripened wherever lightning had entered the ground.

She remembered him holding one against his cheek, listening for thunder inside it.

It had been nineteen years since she had heard her brother’s voice. Usually she could think this without counting them again.

Mara left the apple where it lay. She wheeled her bicycle past the buses, then rode home by the canal, keeping her eyes on the towpath."
